title: how recall decides whether to inject a note (learned gate)
summary: On Claude Code, recall's inject/stay-silent decision is made by a learned gate, not by BM25: EmbeddingGemma 2 q4 scores the prompt+1 prior exchange against note vectors centred on the notes' mean, and a logistic regression over the raw top cosine plus six transcript session facts (shown, opened, written, prompts since compaction, just compacted, anchor files touched) decides; BM25 only answers when the gate is unavailable (no vectors yet, no model, >5 s, error), and Codex/Cursor always use BM25. Note vectors are never computed in the prompt path: a detached refresh job builds them, so a new or edited note gets BM25 recall until it lands.

title: how recall decides whether to inject a note (learned gate)
summary: On Claude Code, recall's inject/stay-silent decision is made by a learned gate, not by BM25: EmbeddingGemma 2 q4 scores the prompt+1 prior exchange against note vectors centred on the notes' mean, and a logistic regression over the raw top cosine plus six transcript session facts decides; BM25 only answers when the gate is unavailable, and Codex/Cursor always use BM25. Since 2026-11-16 both the note vectors and the query vector come from the per-machine embedder daemon: notes are read from the repo's vector store (embedded in the background), the query is one socket request (~55 ms warm; a down daemon is spawned and given 2.5 s, ~1 s measured). A new or edited note without a stored vector yet makes that prompt fall back to BM25 and pings the daemon to embed it. A session's first prompt has NO transcript file yet and is scored as an empty session, not a fallback.
